stations.claim: The moon's pull on the sea raises the tide twice a day.
stations.passage: The moon pulls on the sea, and that pull lifts the tide twice a day.

stations.claim: The harbour fishermen already plan their work around the moon.
stations.passage: The fishermen in our harbour set their nets by the tide tables, so they already plan their work around the moon.

stations.claim: The moon rules every living thing on earth.
stations.passage: The moon therefore rules every living thing on earth, our moods and our sleep included.

stations.claim: The sea may remember the storms that crossed it.
stations.passage: أظن أن البحر يتذكر العواصف التي مرت به
